principles.canonical_identity: Stable canonical IDs and machine keys never change across locales.
principles.effective_corpus: Coverage is measured against the canonical corpus after build-time additions and refreshes, not only against the tracked source snapshot.
principles.semantic_not_literal: Localized prose may adapt wording but must preserve identity, practical meaning, evidence boundaries, uncertainty and safety limits.
principles.evidence_independence: Localization quality never upgrades canonical evidence or recommendation eligibility.
principles.fallback: Human-facing fallback is explicit; machine consumers can always recover canonical identity and source locale.
principles.completion: A locale cannot be called mature solely because every string or slug exists.

release_states.localized-draft: Structural work may exist, but human language review is incomplete.
release_states.language-reviewed: All required localized prose has explicit human language-review state.
release_states.reference-core-complete: The effective canonical knowledge corpus, primary localized surfaces, Search/AI surfaces and deployment gates pass; separately declared non-core surfaces may still use explicit fallback.
release_states.published: All surfaces declared by the locale profile, including required rendered/manual reviews, are complete.

non_automatable_truth: Natural language quality cannot be proven by Cyrillic or token counts.
Cultural fit cannot be proven by route coverage.
Rendered narrow-layout quality needs a rendered review or equivalent browser evidence.
Search ranking, AI citation, traffic and conversion are outcomes, not localization gate results.
